title: API Runtime
html:
Setup · API principles · OpenAPI · Validation

The Fastify API runtime provides configuration, structured logging and tracing, health/lifecycle behavior, the public error envelope, optional PostgreSQL access through Prisma, and optional bearer access-token verification. Product capabilities are modules composed in src/modules.ts. The web application consumes the generated API contract through the workspace SDK package (packages/sdk). The API verifies access tokens; it does not implement login, passwords, refresh tokens, or provider-specific sessions.

Find the owning implementation

Concern Source
Configuration and process composition src/config.ts, src/main.ts
HTTP boundary, lifecycle, and failures src/app.ts, src/lifecycle.ts, src/errors.ts
Module contract and composition src/module.ts, src/modules.ts, src/error-registry.ts
Database client and token verification src/database.ts, src/authentication.ts
Prisma schema, schema meaning, and runtime grants prisma/schema/, prisma/metadata/, prisma/runtime-grants/, reviewed prisma/migrations/
Generated references generate-references.ts, openapi.ts, database-reference.ts
Process smokes scripts/smoke.mjs and module smokes in scripts/smoke/

Modules

A module is one cohesive API capability. It implements the ApiModule contract in src/module.ts: a name, an OpenAPI tag, its requirements (database, authentication), its executable operations, its public error codes, and an activate function that mounts routes once its requirements are configured. Shared runtime files never import a module; src/modules.ts is the only composition point, and dependency rules enforce that boundary.

Keep a module's files together under its name: src/features/<module>/ for domain, application, persistence, contracts, routes, and errors; prisma/schema/<module>.prisma for its models; prisma/metadata/<module>.json for table meaning; prisma/runtime-grants/<module>.sql for least-privilege runtime access; a reviewed migration; tests under test/<module>/; and an optional emitted-process smoke at scripts/smoke/<module>.ts. Follow application boundaries, dependency rules, and the database policies. Orion's reference implementation is a complete example.

Outside production, a module whose requirements are not configured stays unmounted. In production, startup fails instead, so a composed capability cannot silently disappear. Generated OpenAPI and the public error registry always include every composed module, whether or not it is configured locally.

WhatsApp webhook

The WhatsApp module receives Meta callbacks at /webhooks/whatsapp. Development and test can run health-only with this module unconfigured. To mount it, configure restricted PostgreSQL through ORION_DATABASE_URL and provide the three WhatsApp settings from the configuration reference. Generate the callback verification token locally with a cryptographically secure random generator. The app secret and phone number ID come from the Meta dashboard. Keep secrets in ignored environment files or the deployment secret store.

The subscription GET returns the original challenge as plain text after verifying the token. The POST computes HMAC-SHA256 over the exact request bytes before parsing JSON. Supported messages and matching outbound delivery updates for the configured number commit together before acknowledgement. Incoming message IDs deduplicate redelivery. Other numbers and unsupported events are ignored. Enable HTTPS at ingress and omit query strings from ingress logs because Meta sends the verification token in the subscription query.

The inbox accepts text, interactive or template button replies, images, audio and documents. It stores normalized content and media references. The runtime role has only INSERT access to the inbox. Conversation processing and automated retention are tracked in the V1 plan.

Reply dispatch

WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN enables the outbox worker when the webhook and PostgreSQL are configured. It uses the pinned Graph API version from WHATSAPP_GRAPH_API_VERSION. The credential belongs in the deployment secret store with permission to send from the configured business number. Tests supply synthetic credentials and mock the Meta transport.

The conversation flow can enqueue a text or up-to-three-button reply with a stable intent UUID and its service-window deadline. The enqueue operation accepts the current database transaction so the conversation step and reply intent can commit together. It rejects an attempt to reuse the same ID for different content. Claiming a row is conditional and happens before calling Meta. The dispatch limits an attempt to four seconds and honors throttling backoff, including a longer provider retry delay. It retries only an explicit Meta throttle rejection, at most four attempts and within the reply deadline.

A timeout, disconnected response, malformed success, provider server error or abandoned claim can leave an unknown result. The row becomes UNCERTAIN and stays out of dispatch until reconciled by delivery evidence. The signed delivery callback identifies the local intent through the opaque ID or the known Meta message ID. Events can arrive before the send response. Later or repeated weaker events leave confirmed delivery or read status intact. The runtime can update dispatch evidence, and the stored intent stays immutable.

The internal queue entry point is outbox.ts. The conversation flow that creates reply intents and the closure template are separate tasks in the V1 plan. Use test traffic until the operational controls in the plan are in place.

GLPI integration

The server-side GLPI client targets the REST v1 API used by the legacy support channel. Configure the base API URL, the GLPI API-client token and the scoped service-account user token together in the server environment. The configuration reference lists the keys. Use HTTPS for any real instance. HTTP is permitted on loopback in development and test. The transport rejects redirects.

The user token is sent only to initSession. Requests with an established session use the application token and session token. Concurrent calls share session initialization. A directory read refreshes and retries once after GLPI explicitly rejects an expired session. The runtime and reverse proxy should exclude query strings, request bodies and authentication headers from logs because directory queries carry corporate email addresses.

Directory lookup pages through search/User, verifies the entire normalized email against returned addresses, and checks the active flag. It accepts exactly one active GLPI user ID. Multiple matching users, incomplete or inconsistent pagination, and provider errors return distinct internal outcomes. The employee identity workflow will use neutral replies and verify mailbox ownership before linking an account.

Ticket creation uses the supplied GLPI requester ID and escapes the plain-text description for GLPI's HTML field. A confirmed creation includes the positive ticket ID from GLPI. A known denial can be distinguished from a timeout, lost response or malformed success after dispatch. The client sends each write only once. The ticket workflow will persist the creation intent and reconcile uncertain outcomes before any further attempt.

The adapter is covered by synthetic contract and transport tests. The employee verification and ticket workflows are tracked in the V1 plan. Live testing requires the scoped service account in PH-08.

GLPI REST v1 reference · GLPI User search fields

Employee email verification

The identity service establishes mailbox control for a WhatsApp sender and one GLPI user. It queries the directory only for configured corporate domains and issues a code only after a unique active match. The sender scope includes the WhatsApp business phone ID and prefers the Meta business-scoped sender ID. Phone-only senders use their phone identifier. A changed sender scope requires verification.

One reservation permits one SMTP submission. A code has the prefix MNS- and expires after ten minutes. Each challenge permits five attempts. The sender and mailbox each allow three reservations in a rolling hour. Repeated inbound message IDs cannot consume another attempt or trigger another email. Reserving a new challenge supersedes the previous one. Consuming a code and creating the verified link commit together. The link expires after thirty days.

The webhook stores a keyed digest for a standalone verification code and removes complete code mentions from other message text. Challenges and mailbox quotas also use keyed digests. Rotating the key invalidates pending codes and starts new mailbox quota counters. Issuing the code and querying GLPI happen outside database locks. The conversation flow must durably enqueue the same neutral acknowledgement before doing any directory or mail work. That rule keeps mailbox eligibility and SMTP outcomes out of the response. A failed or unconfirmed relay response does not cause an automatic resend. The employee can make a new request within the quota.

Configure the seven IDENTITY_* settings as a group with GLPI. Generate the 32-byte secret with a cryptographically secure random generator and place it with the relay credentials in the server secret store. The SMTP adapter uses implicit TLS on port 465 and requires STARTTLS on other ports, with normal certificate verification. Keep the identity service internal. The bot menu and processing of the stored verification event remain tracked in the V1 plan.

Local commands

Use setup for the frozen install, generated Prisma client, environment loading, containers, and startup order. pnpm -C apps/api dev loads the ignored root .env.local when present; start runs emitted code and expects its process environment without loading that file.

From the repository root:

Purpose Command
Generate ignored Prisma client pnpm -C apps/api db:generate
Apply committed migrations to the configured database pnpm -C apps/api db:migrate:deploy
Check API behavior/types pnpm -C apps/api test and pnpm -C apps/api typecheck
Emit/start API pnpm -C apps/api build, then pnpm -C apps/api start
Intentionally regenerate tracked API/database/configuration/error references pnpm -C apps/api references:write
Check current API/database/SDK references without editing them pnpm references:check

Tests and reference generation use fresh migrated Testcontainers PostgreSQL, so a compatible container runtime must be reachable. Follow the artifact workflow for downstream SDK/portal generation after source changes. The root pnpm validate also checks emitted builds, real-process recovery, and browser behavior; a focused package check alone does not replace it.

Configuration and database access

config.ts is the sole runtime environment parser; the generated configuration reference owns the setting catalog. ORION_ENV is always required. ORION_DATABASE_URL enables the database for modules that require it and adds a bounded database check to readiness. ORION_TOKEN_ISSUER, ORION_TOKEN_AUDIENCE, and ORION_TOKEN_JWKS_URL enable bearer authentication and must be configured together.

ORION_DATABASE_URL is the restricted runtime credential. Only the Prisma CLI reads ORION_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL, supplied separately for migration commands; the CLI does not automatically load the API's root .env.local. Keep both out of tracked files and do not leave the migration credential in the runtime environment.

The runtime role needs USAGE on the application schema plus only the table and column privileges that each module declares in prisma/runtime-grants/. It needs no DDL grant. The database fixture provisions separate migration/runtime roles and applies those grants, so integration tests run with the same least-privilege runtime role.

The release workflow owns durable migration recording. An empty registry is not permission to rewrite unverified history.

Identity and contract

The shared token verifier accepts verified at+jwt tokens signed with RS256 or ES256 by the configured issuer for the configured audience. It validates expiration and requires nonempty sub, valid issuance/expiry timing, a stable orion_principal_id UUID, orion_actor_type=human, and a string scope. It yields the principal ID and the issuer-granted scopes; each module maps scopes to its own capabilities. Stored ownership must survive provider changes; request bodies cannot grant identity or capability. The authentication policy and ADR-0012 govern this boundary; no concrete provider is selected or provisioned.

Executable module contracts own operations, stable operation IDs, typed inputs/outputs, and expected failures. The OpenAPI reference includes health and every composed module's operations; the error reference derives from the shared and module registries.

Request protection

A module that exposes authenticated routes should apply request limiting before token verification and database access, as the reference module does with a process-local source-IP limit; health probes stay outside it. Exhaustion returns 429 RATE_LIMITED in the public envelope with a bounded Retry-After. This is resource protection, not a product quota.

Process-local limiting uses the direct peer address; trusted proxies are not configured. A multi-replica or reverse-proxy deployment must define shared/edge limiting and trusted client-IP handling before promising fleet-wide or per-user limits.

Lifecycle and diagnostics

main.ts validates configuration, initializes Pino/OpenTelemetry, then dynamically imports Fastify, Prisma, and composed modules before listening. Preserve that order for instrumented infrastructure. Incoming W3C trace context propagates; each request receives a fresh server-generated x-request-id. Errors follow the public envelope. Logs and traces identify the service by the API package name.

Startup reports initialization, liveness reports process-local health, and readiness becomes unavailable while draining or when a configured database is unavailable. A configured database is probed before readiness and through a bounded readiness check. SIGINT/SIGTERM trigger bounded HTTP, database, and telemetry shutdown.

Logs and exported spans/metric dimensions use allowlisted operational fields. The runtime does not log payloads, raw URLs, headers, configuration objects, or arbitrary exception messages. Unexpected failures produce one sanitized diagnostic occurrence. A readiness failure or a lost response cannot prove that a prior write failed; see delivery and side effects.
